sentences.span: Yields have pared back some of that rise this morning, trading 2-3bps lower across the curve.
sentences.why: The 25bp hike and higher neutral-rate/long-run dot are correctly sourced (GS 16688, JPM 16690: median neutral dot rose 3.06%->3.25%), but the day's rates note puts the 10yr at 5.00% this morning (10yr Treasury @ 5.00, having hit a post-2007 high of 5.02% on the decision), not 4.95%. The sentence understates the yield by ~5-7bp and frames it as 'back' to a lower level when the source shows only a 2-3bp pare-back from a fresh high.

No document in the day's source set covers an August 31 TLT call or a 10-year level from that date (the set only covers Sept 15-17). The claim is about the pulse's own prior editorial position with a retrospective yield level, and nothing in the provided PDFs supports or contradicts a 'just under 5%' 10-year reading as of August 31.

sentences.span: For our part we continue to look for one more hike at the December meeting, in line with the revised median FOMC expectations.
sentences.why: JPMorgan (16690) explicitly calls the next hike for December while Goldman (16688) explicitly calls it for October (see s4/s5); both keep the same terminal-rate framing. 'Two largest houses' diverging on timing while agreeing on the endpoint is a fair characterization of the two documents read together.

sentences.span: Market pricing of the probability of further hikes this year rose 8pp to 51% for October and 9pp to 78% for December today
sentences.why: Goldman's own note states 'We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October' and separately cites the 51% October pricing figure, matching the sentence's figure and attribution exactly.

sentences.span: The median GDP outlook for '26 and '27 was revised up a tenth...unemployment rate forecasts also became more optimistic, this year revised down to 4.1%
sentences.why: JPMorgan's note states it looks for the second hike in December, and separately notes GDP forecasts revised up and the 2026 unemployment-rate forecast revised down to 4.1% -- all three claims in the sentence are directly supported.

sentences.span: We have kept our forecast of the terminal rate unchanged at 3.25-3.5%
sentences.why: Goldman's note keeps the terminal rate at 3.25-3.5% and adds 'a third 25bp cut in March 2028' to reach it, matching both the range and the 2028 third-cut detail in the sentence.

No document in the provided Sept 16-17 set contains the Yanbu 1.1mb/d-vs-4mb/d figures or the Saudi production 6.2mb/d-from-10.9mb/d figures. The day's oil coverage (ING 16619, GS 16596/16597) mentions Yanbu qualitatively (suspended shipments, loss of flow) but none give these specific barrel counts.

sentences.span: EU gas storage is a little over 68% full, well below the seasonal 5-year average of 84%.
sentences.why: ING's note gives the 68%-vs-84% gas storage figures verbatim and separately describes the ICE gasoil crack (a diesel-margin proxy) as 'near record levels' above $80/bbl, supporting the diesel-margin claim and the ING attribution.

No document in the set frames the AI selloff as an intra-theme rotation rather than an exit; the closest AI-capex documents (UBS 'Frontier pacing calls' 16636/16637/16642) don't use this rotation-vs-exit framing, and no other source in the set does either.

The only Bank of America document in the set (16570, Capital Market Outlook Sept 14) is a markets-in-review letter with no S&P 500 target and no rotation calls. No 7,800 target or BofA rotation-call content appears anywhere in the day's source set (the only S&P target found, 8,100/8,400, is from UBS, a different bank, in 16641).

Neither $AHR nor $WELL, nor the $71/$292 targets, nor any REIT/landlord pricing-power call appears anywhere in the provided source-text files for either date.
